name: Iron Manuscript

civilization.name: The Ferroglyphic Compact
civilization.notes: An industrious civilization that carves its history and laws into massive iron plates, viewing metalwork as the highest form of expression and governance.

description: Iron Manuscript is a dense, metal-rich world where ferrous deposits have stained the continents in bands of oxide red, magnetite black, and pyrite gold. The exposed planetary core is visible at the bottom of an equatorial canyon system so vast it can be seen from orbit, its molten glow painting the canyon walls in shifting patterns of orange and white. Mountain ranges bristle with natural iron spires formed by volcanic extrusion, standing like rows of dark monuments against a steel-grey sky.

The higher-than-average gravity gives everything a weighty, grounded quality that visitors notice immediately in their movements and breathing. The air tastes faintly of metal, and magnetic fields are strong enough to affect unshielded electronics. The Ferroglyphic Compact has built their cities into the mountain spires themselves, carving vast chambers and connecting them with iron bridges that sing in harmonic resonance when the wind passes through.

The Compact's written history extends back roughly four thousand years, all of it preserved on iron plates that line the walls of their deepest archives. They regard the monolithic structures found on three continents—predating their civilization by an estimated fifty thousand years—as sacred texts from a divine author. Their industrial revolution has been driven primarily by the desire to build tools capable of deciphering these ancient works.

Human contact teams have established cautious diplomatic relations with the Compact, who view off-worlders with scholarly curiosity rather than fear. The planet's extraordinary metal reserves have attracted mining interests, creating a diplomatic tension between exploitation and the Compact's sovereignty. The monoliths themselves may hold the key to the relationship—preliminary analysis suggests they were inscribed by the same unknown agency responsible for similar structures found on Gilded Grimoire, hinting at a connection that spans star systems.
